events.what: Dynnikov reduces ZCC to standard polyhedra (Theorem 2.5/1.4) and proves ZCC for polyhedra embeddable in 3-manifolds (Theorem 1.5)
Fagan, Qiu and Wang relate the stable Andrews-Curtis conjecture to fake surfaces and prove the complexity < 6 case of that reformulation

judgement.doubts: The record states that Theorem 1.5 relies on a transfer of Matveev's 1987 technique that the paper asserts rather than re-verifies; no expert reading found yet. The reduction to standard polyhedra alone would be scope none (a reduction), but Theorem 1.5 settles a class of complexes (those embeddable in 3-manifolds, including non-standard ones) affirmatively, which is a case of the bullet.

corrections.why: F3: the record's own summary says Theorem 1.5 proves ZCC 'holds for polyhedra embeddable in 3-manifolds' — a class of the bullet's contractible 2-complexes settled affirmatively, i.e. a case, not a bound; the competing_reading argued this and was rejected only on framing grounds. Unreviewed status does not lower a case below partial.
F14: a partial row carries the direction of its event; Theorem 1.5 confirms collapsibility on the settled class.
